contradictionsAndDeadEnds: The dispatch restates `district-miss refusals 9,510`. That number is EXACT and it already includes the 1,026 parcels that carry a district in a city with no table at all: 49,855 no-table-city parcels + 8,484 table-city parcels = 58,339 = P-326's denominator, and P-326's measured districtOnFile per county sums to 9,510. Reading it as 9,510 + 1,026 double-counts the 1,026. A live run will still MOVE counts between buckets against the pre-fix store, because pre-fix those 1,026 were written the city's no-table `unaccounted` answer; the total does not change.

The 40-city roll-up's class (a) 45,138 and P-300's class (a) 44,112 differ by exactly 1,026 for the same reason: the roll-up counts every parcel in a class (a) city, P-300 counts only the district-less ones.

class (b) is two cities, not one. Gholson (840) is coded; Thrall (487) is not, so the class (b) value expectation is 840 today and 1,327 only after Thrall's row is coded. Thrall's 487 stay `unaccounted` and are counted as `defaultRowMissing` -- they are not a value and not a refusal.

DEAD-END: running the falsifier suite against the pre-change writer to get the pre-change evidence does not work -- it imports constants this lane adds, so it fails to LOAD (SyntaxError: does not provide an export named 'CLASS_UNZONED_CITY_WIDE_LINE'). A separate probe importing only shared APIs is the instrument that can actually show both directions.

DEAD-END: `git stash push -- src test scripts` does not make the tree pre-change -- package.json/package-lock.json are outside those paths, so the stash aborts and the probe silently runs against the NEW code. The pre-change transcript was produced by stashing the two src files by name, and the transcription is only trusted because the corpus version printed in it reads 1.4.0.

DEAD-END: PowerShell writes UTF-16 with a BOM through `>` and Out-File, which makes JSON artifacts unreadable to node's JSON.parse. Artifacts were written with [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText(..., UTF8Encoding(false)).

threeQuestionGate.whatExecutes: the classification is DATA (city-setback-classification.json, built by scripts/build-p300-city-classification.mjs) read by citySetbackClassificationFor; the default is DATA (the corpus's jurisdiction-default row) reached only through resolveJurisdictionDefault; the writer branch (processCityPage) executes both.
threeQuestionGate.whatTriggers: the city's row in the table plus the parcel's own zoningDistrict cell. A district on file triggers the district path (ruling 6); no district on file triggers the city's class.
threeQuestionGate.whatFails: (1) A zoned city's parcel receiving a default VALUE: class (a) parcels get a refusal, never a value, and FALSIFIER 2a asserts it. (2) A district-miss parcel receiving an unnamed refusal: the refusal names the district code AND the city AND says to verify with the city, asserted both in the factory test and in the ledger policy's signature match. (3) A city the tables leave unclassified receiving a guessed class: FALSIFIER 2null. (4) An absence with no instrument behind it: assertNoFalseAbsence admits only the class (c) shape, with its basis, on the allowlisted rails.
whatBypasses: a hand UPDATE against parcel_record_cell: outside this code entirely; the ledger policy's reason census would see an unmatched refusal as an open rail, which is the only available signal

a city added to the corpus without a classification row: the generator THROWS ('no classification row for <key>') rather than defaulting; a city added to the store's roster but not to the 40 gets no class, so it stays `unaccounted`

a zoning layer acquired later for a class (a) city: the class (a) refusal is sticky. The moment the layer exists, the parcels have districts and are district-carried, so the refusal is the correct terminal state for what was on file when it was written; releasing it is P-364's job (the class's own acquisition row, which opens the class in the ledger policy)
a corpus version bump that renames a signature: the reason text would stop matching and the rail would OPEN (loud), not silently pass
